instructions: Thaw the puff pastry in the fridge overnight, or on the counter for about 40 minutes. It should be cold but bend without cracking.
In a small bowl, stir together the sugar and cinnamon.
Unfold the pastry on a lightly floured counter and roll it lightly into an even rectangle. Sprinkle the cinnamon sugar over it, then roll lightly again to press it in.
Roll the two short ends toward the middle so they meet, keeping both rolls the same size.
Wrap the roll and chill it in the fridge for about 30 minutes.
Meanwhile, heat the oven to 375°F and line a baking sheet with parchment.
Slice the chilled roll into pieces 1/4 to 1/3 inch thick. Lay them cut side up on the sheet, with a little space between them.
Bake for about 10 minutes. Flip each cookie and bake for 5 to 10 minutes, until golden.
Transfer the palmiers to a wire rack to cool. They keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 3 days.
advance_prep_notes: chill the rolled dough for 30 minutes before slicing
method_notes: None of the versions has 20 ratings, so this follows An Italian in My Kitchen (4.73 from 11): one sheet of pastry rolled with cinnamon sugar, chilled, sliced and flipped halfway. Taste of Home (10 reviews, no score) uses sugar alone and more of it, frozen firm before slicing. The thawing times come from Dessert Now, Dinner Later, and the 3-day keeping time from America's Test Kitchen's listing. Makes about 25.
